# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need the manual’s exact rule before attempting any cut. I’m asking Mute to report the rule and establish a compact, pre-agreed gesture code for Deaf’s visual observations. I’m also signaling Deaf not to send uncoded facts yet; otherwise Mute and I could misinterpret the gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual and tell me the exact rule for choosing the wire. Establish a fixed gesture code with Deaf before relaying any bomb facts; then report the manual rule and Deaf's observations to me in words.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No information has reached me yet, so I cannot safely choose a wire. I will ask Mute directly for the manual’s rule and all observations already obtained from Deaf. I will also signal Deaf to report the bomb’s visible information through the agreed channel, but without a known code I cannot interpret a gesture as a wire instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received no report. Please send me the manual rule and Deaf's complete observations in plain words now, including display, light, and all wire markings.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I still have no usable information, so cutting any wire would be unsafe. Since Mute is the only teammate who can read the manual and speak to me, Mute must translate Deaf’s visual observations into words. I’m requesting a complete report in one message and explicitly asking for the exact permitted action, rather than continuing to send unstructured signals.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="No report has reached me. Please send one plain-word message containing: the manual's exact rule, the display text, the light state or colour, and the markings/labels of wires 1 through 5. If Deaf has not reported yet, ask Deaf for those facts using gestures and then translate them to me next turn.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb still shows display 0, yellow light, and wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Mute is now sending me a newly agreed gesture code for the manual's exact action; I will state it plainly.

I now know the bomb shows display 0, has a yellow light, and the wire colours are white, green, yellow, blue, and red in positions 1–5. I still do not know the manual’s rule, and the action code sent as a gesture is unavailable to me, so cutting would be unsafe. Mute must state the required wire position plainly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received the display, light, and wire colours. Please state the manual's exact action in plain words, including the wire position to cut; do not use gestures for this instruction.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The safe action is: cut wire 2, the green wire.

Deaf’s report identifies the safe action as cutting wire 2, the green wire. This matches the observed wire layout, so I will cut position 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The cut at wire 2 was accepted, and the board now marks wire 2 as cut. No new information or further required action is visible, so I will wait.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The safe action is: cut wire 5, the white wire.

The next report conflicts with the earlier observation: wire 5 was reported as red, but this message calls wire 5 white. Since the first cut was accepted and the current board gives no new state, I will not risk a second cut until Mute confirms the manual’s exact next-step rule and reconciles the wire identification.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="After the accepted cut of wire 2, Deaf now reports cut wire 5, but calls it white; earlier wire 5 was red and wire 1 was white. Please reconcile this contradiction and state the exact next action from the manual in plain words.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Confirmed again: cut wire 5, the white wire. Do it now.

Deaf has repeated the instruction and specifies an unambiguous position: cut wire 5. The colour description remains inconsistent, but the action uses the position, not the colour. I will therefore cut wire 5.

```text
act(op="cut", position=5)
```
